newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 23.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- SUPPORT FOR PACT TO ENSURE EMU STABILITY

European finance ministers meeting in Dublin over the weekend are reported to have reached agreement in principle on a stability pact aimed at securing fiscal discipline after the creation of the single currency. Agreement was also reached on the subject of a new exchange rate mechanism that will regulate relations between the euro and the currencies of those states not initially taking part. The meeting was seen by observers as an attempt to signal to financial markets that Emu remains on track.
-- BASS RIVALS LOOK FOR MERGER CONCESSIONS

It is reported that rivals of brewing group Bass believe that the company will have to make changes to its acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley if it is to secure regulatory approval for the deal. Rivals believe that the increase in the company's share of the market to 35-38 percent will have an impact on beer prices. At present the Office of Fair Trading is in the process of canvassing opinion from the industry on the Bass plans.
-- LABOUR FACES SETBACK ON CAPITAL GAINS TAX PLANS

It is reported that during the coming week the Confederation of British Industry and the National Association of Pension Funds will express their concerns about Labour plans to introduce a two-tier capital gains tax system. The position of the CBI on the issue is of particular importance to the party, given the group's previous support for the approach being taken to reform in this area. Labour, meanwhile, has stressed that as yet it is not fully committed to the plan and will listen to any criticism levelled.
-- ONE-2-ONE CHIEF PLANS AGGRESSIVE CAMPAIGN

It is believed that the new chief executive of Mercury One- 2-One will next month begin aggressively marketing the company's mobile telecoms services in outlets such as supermarkets, chemists and DIY stores. Jan Peters, formerly with US West, is keen to see aggressive marketing techniques which proved successful in the US applied in Britain. She believes easier access to mobile services will result in subscriber numbers increasing.
-- LAL BID SPURS LLOYDS TSB TO TACKLE OVERLAP

It is expected that Lloyds Bank, in making clear its plans for the acquisition of the 37 percent of Lloyds Abbey Life that it does not already own, will also address the rationalisation that will need to take place within the group's overlapping insurance activities. A number of other players in the insurance market are also believed to have examined possible bids for Abbey Life, which is a separate unit of Lloyds Abbey Life.
-- EU LOOKS TO EXTEND LAWS ON WORKER CONSULTATION

New rules to be outlined on Tuesday by European Commissioner Padraig Flynn would force companies with more than 50 staff to engage in consultations with workers on group affairs. It is expected that these proposals will be met with opposition from some business groups as well as the British government, which already has an opt-out from an EU directive that comes into force on Monday obliging larger companies to form works councils.
-- UNIONS TO PRESS 800 EU COMPANIES TO SET UP WORKS COUNCILS

European trade unions are reported to be planning to target some 800 multinational companies in their attempt to secure the setting up of works councils, as set out in an EU directive that has now come into force. Already an estimated 20 percent of companies covered by the legislation have voluntarily established such consultation bodies, from Monday such action will be obligatory under law.
-- OFTEL U-TURN ON PRICE CUTS ADDS TO BT COSTS

BT is reported to be furious over a letter received late on Friday from the industry regulator Oftel telling it not to implement a planned price-cutting package for companies wishing to connect to high-speed ISDN services. The company, which warns that reversing its own plans for the price cuts will take time, also notes that it has spent hundreds of thousands of pounds marketing the services. Oftel has revealed that it took the action after receiving complaints late in the day from BT competitors.
-- TELEPHONE BANKING WINS 125,000 USERS A MONTH

A report from market research group Datamonitor reveals that 125,000 new customers are signing up each month to telephone banking services in the UK. By the end of the decade it expects some 30 percent of the population to make use of such services. Much of the popularity of telephone banking has been attributed to the success of the First Direct service offered by Midland Bank. All of the major high street banks now provide telephone banking options.
-- NON-SALARY PAY FOR TOP EXECUTIVES ON THE RISE

A new report from consultants New Bridge Street Consultants reveals that directors of some of Britain's top companies are receiving a higher proportion of their overall remuneration via non-salary means such as bonuses and share options. Those with the 30 largest companies according to market capitalization are currently receiving average total packages worth 493,005 stg annually - of which 37 percent of the total being non-salary.
